item.title: GlobeTopper faces up to $2.5 million in lost revenue after hackers steal $70,000 in gift cards
item.description: According to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), parent company iQSTEL said GlobeTopper detected the intrusion on October 22 and took the platform offline the next morning after spotting further unauthorized activity.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for AI Code Review
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Ship, a beta AI suite that reviews pull requests, fixes issues, and approves changes per team policies. It merges code review, automated fixes, and policy enforcement to speed development while preserving quality. Deploying Claude Ship into CI/CD pipelines lets teams set approval thresholds and monitor false positives for safe integration.

item.title: Microsoft Uncovers Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities in Azure
item.description: Microsoft identified multiple Linux kernel flaws in Azure that could allow attackers to compromise affected systems. The vulnerabilities affect IPv4 networking, Ethernet bridge, Netfilter, SCTP, and XFRM subsystems, and are catalogued as CVE-2026-64564, CVE-2026-98432, and CVE-2026-99999, potentially enabling remote code execution. Administrators should apply the latest kernel updates or install the provided patches to eliminate the exploitation vector.

item.title: Top Attack Path Management Tools Ranked for 2026
item.description: Cyber Security News evaluated defensive tools, ranking the top ten attack path management solutions available in 2026. These tools analyze complex attack chains by converting vulnerability lists into graphs mapping misconfigurations, excessive permissions, and credential reuse. Security teams can deploy attack path management software to identify critical choke points and remediate high-risk operational vectors efficiently.

item.title: Hackers Plant Backdoors in 6 WordPress Plugins to Steal Passwords and Take Over Websites
item.description: Hackers planted a remote-control backdoor in nine versions of six WordPress plugins from WP connect on November 22, 2026. The malware could let an attacker steal password hashes, run commands, and take over a website. But WordPress.org blocked the tainted versions before distributing them and closed all six plugins that evening.

item.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Flaw Enables Remote Brake Control
item.description: A critical Bluetooth flaw in Elecbrakes trailer brake controllers, CVE-2026-96805, lets attackers within range manipulate brakes without pairing. Rated 9.6 CVSS, the flaw exploits command injection in Bluetooth, enabling unauthenticated remote brake control. Manufacturers should push firmware updates disabling unsecured Bluetooth commands; users must avoid exposing controllers to untrusted devices until patched.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Security Update for MariaDB
item.description: Red Hat released a security update addressing security flaws in the mariadb:11.8 module for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. Red Hat Product Security rated the operational impact of these vulnerabilities as Important based on Common Vulnerability Scoring System metrics. System administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102830 advisory updates to mitigate potential exploitation risks across enterprise RHEL environments.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important WebKit2GTK3 Update
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for webkit2gtk3 on RHEL 9.2 for SAP Solutions. The patch addresses undisclosed vulnerabilities that could enable code execution or system compromise, with CVSS scores linked in the CVE references and mitigate potential privilege escalation. Administrators should apply the update immediately to eliminate the exploitation vector.

item.title: Hackers Compromise Check Point Management Servers
item.description: Hackers have compromised Check Point Security Management Servers, which store firewall rule sets that govern corporate traffic filtering. The ongoing campaign has affected at least 22 organizations worldwide, and attackers retain active access to many servers, exposing critical network controls. Check Point recommends applying the latest firmware patches, disabling unused management interfaces, and monitoring for anomalous configuration changes.

item.title: Google Cloud CISO Discusses Agentic AI in SOC
item.description: Google Cloud CISO Chris Betz spoke about agentic AI in security operations during a Help Net Security interview. He noted that automation lets attackers traverse networks in minutes, questioned junior analyst roles, and urged reassessment of controls and board oversight. Betz advised organizations to evolve SOC workflows with AI-driven threat hunting and governance to counter increasingly stealthy espionage groups.

item.title: Ransomware Groups Multiply Despite Fewer Victim Payments
item.description: Check Point Research’s State of Ransomware Q3 2026 report lists 2,830 victims on data-leak sites, the highest quarterly total on record. July, August, and September accounted for 964, 1,042, and 824 victims respectively, indicating a sustained expansion of active ransomware groups. The report shows declining payments but continued brand proliferation, stressing the need for stronger defensive measures.

item.title: AWS European Sovereign Cloud: Architecture and Compliance Overview
item.description: AWS European Sovereign Cloud offers infrastructure designed to meet European data sovereignty requirements, providing isolated regions and compliance with local regulations. The architecture provides physical and logical separation, encryption controls, and audit capabilities, enabling organizations to retain full data control while leveraging AWS services. Customers can evaluate the platform against certifications and compliance frameworks to determine suitability for sensitive workloads.

item.title: SplitSecure Unveils Secret-Splitting Access Control Platform
item.description: SplitSecure announced a new access control platform built on secret-splitting technology to replace password managers, PAM, and vaults. The architecture supports passwords, passkeys, one-time codes, SAML & OIDC federation, and SSH, enabling secure credential handling for humans and AI agents. Organizations should evaluate the platform for integration with existing identity systems and assess its impact on compliance and operational workflows.

item.title: OpenAI, Cisco Launch AI-Assisted Linux Shield Tool
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco unveiled Shirudo, an AI-assisted Linux runtime that deploys temporary eBPF controls to block exploit behaviors before patches. The system generates programs that intercept vulnerable system calls, preventing exploitation without rebooting and narrowing the exposure window. Deploy Shirudo on exposed hosts, monitor logs, and apply vendor patches promptly to eliminate the root flaw.

item.title: CISA Adds Actively Exploited N-able MailAssure SSRF Flaw to KEV Catalog
item.description: CISA added the critical SSRF vulnerability CVE-2026-134624 in N-able MailAssure's LDAP synchronization to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, confirming active exploitation. The flaw allows authenticated attackers to force server-side requests to internal resources, enabling data exposure and lateral movement within protected networks. Administrators must immediately apply N-able's patch and enforce strict LDAP restrictions to mitigate the SSRF risk.

item.title: OpenAI, Cisco Release Shirudo to Shield Linux Until Patches
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, a Linux runtime that deploys temporary eBPF controls to block exploit behaviors while patches are pending. Shirudo generates small programs that intercept vulnerable system calls, preventing exploitation without rebooting and narrowing the exposure window. Deploy Shirudo on exposed hosts, monitor logs, and apply vendor patches promptly to eliminate the root flaw.

item.title: Node.js simple-git RCE Vulnerability CVE-2026-134815
item.description: A critical flaw in the Node.js simple-git library allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands on servers that pass untrusted input into Git arguments. Tracked as CVE-2026-134815, the vulnerability is an argument injection weakness present in simple-git versions before 4.1.0, enabling remote code execution without authentication. Users should upgrade to simple-git 4.1.0 or later to mitigate the flaw.

item.title: IT Delegates Password Management While Maintaining Control
item.description: IT departments often delegate password management to business units, creating accounts that may be unknown to central security teams. This practice can leave IT responsible for credentials it cannot monitor, increasing risk when personnel changes or external contractors access shared accounts. Implementing centralized identity governance, enforcing least-privilege access, and requiring IT involvement in account provisioning can mitigate these risks.

item.title: Stalwart 1.2.0 Adds Full Exchange Protocol Support
item.description: Stalwart 1.2.0 introduces full Exchange-compatible protocols, enabling MAPI over HTTP, EWS, ActiveSync, and Autodiscover for Outlook, Apple Mail, and mobile clients. The open-source mail server ships under the AGPL Community edition, offering mail, calendar, contacts, tasks, and notes. Administrators can deploy Stalwart as a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange, but should evaluate compatibility with existing client configurations before migration.

Security teams should deploy Shirudo immediately to mitigate known exploits and reduce patch deployment windows.

item.title: Ongoing Scanning Detected on BANATSYNC Subnet
item.description: SANS Internet Storm Center reports continuous scanning from subnet 109.160.32.0/24, assigned to BANATSYNC SRL, a Romanian web hosting and VPS provider. DShield sensor data shows persistent probing over 90 days, suggesting ongoing reconnaissance or potential exploitation attempts against the subnet's hosts. Security teams should monitor for suspicious activity, enforce rate limiting, and harden hosts to mitigate potential threats.

item.title: GTA VI Hacker Sentenced, Released Same Day
item.description: A British cybercriminal breached Rockstar Games’ systems, leaking unreleased Grand Theft Auto VI footage in the United Kingdom. The attack exploited internal access controls, but no specific vulnerability was publicly disclosed without evidence of ongoing threat to Rockstar’s operations. He received a seven-year prison sentence and was released on license after serving time.

item.title: USN-9189-1: Qt5Compat vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Qt5Compat did not correctly handle certain text codec names, which could lead to an out-of-bounds read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service.
